name: VPN - Connect and Verify HTB Lab Access
description: Connect your attack VM to the HTB lab network via OpenVPN. Requires sudo because creating a TUN interface needs root-level network manipulation. After connecting, verify tun0 exists and the routing table has the lab range before touching any target.

variations.description: Connect with a named .ovpn file (OSCP lab style)
variations.label: sudo openvpn

examples.label: Expected tun0 IP and route
examples.command:
# tun0 -> 10.10.x.2 (VPN subnet)
# Route: 10.129.0.0/16 via tun0 -> lab access confirmed

notes:
sudo is required because establishing a VPN tunnel requires root-level network interface manipulation. The user.ovpn file downloaded from the HTB platform acts as both configuration and authentication key.

Two verification steps: first, ip -4 a show tun0 (or ifconfig) confirms a tun0 adapter was created with an IP in the HTB VPN range. Second, netstat -rn confirms the routing table routes 10.129.0.0/16 through tun0 via gateway 10.10.14.1. If either is absent, the connection did not fully establish.

The HTB VPN enforces single-session use per account — connecting from a second machine will drop both sessions. Common source of confusion when switching between Pwnbox and a local VM.

The HTB VPN is a lab access mechanism only, not a privacy tool. Keep client assessment data out of any VM also used for HTB practice. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 2.

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux

recommended.note: Once VPN is confirmed, start scanning the target.
